channel.title: GeoPulse. Geopolitics in brief
channel.description: Signal-first briefings on geopolitics, edited by Lavkesh Dwivedi.

item.title: Flydubai Passenger Recounts Saving Stabbed Pilot
item.description: A Georgian-Israeli dentist on a Flydubai flight from Dubai to Israel helped a pilot allegedly stabbed by his co-pilot on September 30. Shota Musayev left his wife to assist the injured crew member. He feared for his own survival during the incident. The flight was diverted to safety. Georgian-Israeli dentist Shota Musayev told RFE/RL that he feared he might not survive when he left his wife’s side to help after the lead pilot was allegedly stabbed by his co-pilot during a Flydubai flight from Dubai to Israel on September 30.

item.title: WHO appeals for massive aid influx ahead of winter
item.description: The World Health Organization warned that delayed medical supplies to Gaza risk devastating consequences. Lifesaving medicines and prosthetics are stuck in transit from Israel. The UN agency appealed for a massive aid influx before winter arrives. Palestinians in the enclave urgently need these critical resources. Repeated delays in bringing lifesaving medicines, prosthetics and more from Israel into Gaza risk having devastating consequences on Palestinians who urgently need them in the war-torn enclave, the UN World Health Organization (WHO) said on Friday.

item.title: Row erupts over Cairo mural depicting Tutankhamun and Nefertiti with dark skin
item.description: Cairo authorities removed a 66-metre mural from Tahrir Square before Xi Jinping’s state visit. The artwork depicted Tutankhamun and Nefertiti with dark skin. Critics alleged it revived Afrocentric claims about Pharaohs’ origins. The removal sparked a public row over historical representation. Artwork created in Tahrir Square for Chinese president’s state visit to Egypt is painted over amid allegations it revived Afrocentric claims about Pharaohs’ originsOn the eve of Chinese president Xi Jinping’s state visit to Cairo last month, the city authorities were busy removing a 66-metre-long mural from the esteemed guest’s line of sight. item.title: After Russia's Elections, An Expert On Fraud Is Arrested And Reportedly Beaten
item.description: Russian security forces detained fraud analyst Aleksandr Kynev in Moscow after he warned of vote falsifications benefiting United Russia. He was reportedly beaten while in custody. The incident highlights a clash between security agencies and political operatives within the Kremlin. In the days between the elections and his arrest, Aleksandr Kynev had pointed to evidence of falsifications benefitting the United Russia party.

item.title: US blast simulation targets China’s alleged secret nuke testing
item.description: The US Department of Energy conducted underground blast experiments in Nevada. These tests aim to detect clandestine nuclear detonations. The program addresses concerns about China's secret testing capabilities. Faced with rising great-power suspicions and the challenge of verifying clandestine, cavity-muffled detonations, the US is turning to high-precision subterranean blast experiments in the Nevada desert to strip covert nuclear testing of its technical cover.

item.title: The Bolsonaros…they’re back! Brazil heads to the polls – podcast
item.description: Brazil held its first-round presidential election on Sunday. Flávio Bolsonaro, son of the jailed former president, ran to succeed his father. Jair Bolsonaro was convicted in September 2025 of attempting a coup. The campaign tested whether his political legacy survived the conviction. The Bolsonarosthey’re back! Brazil heads to the polls – podcast. The Bolsonarosthey’re back!

item.title: Brazil attorney general says meddling ‘cannot be tolerated’ after Trump funding plans revealed
item.description: Jorge Messias calls Guardian report ‘an important alert for Brazilian sovereignty’ as nation prepares to go to pollsBrazil’s attorney general has said foreign meddling in his country’s institutions and democracy “cannot be tolerated” after a Guardian report revealed how the Trump administration was pushing to direct funds to a campaign against the Brazilian supreme court. Writing on X, Jorge Messia Brazil attorney general says meddling ‘cannot be tolerated’ after Trump funding plans revealed.

item.title: Kyrgyz Activist Gets 2 Years For Criticizing Growing Chinese Presence
item.description: The Lenin District Court in Bishkek found activist and politician Mavlyan Askarbekov guilty and sentenced to two years in prison on offenses related to a law on incitement of racial, ethnic, national, religious, or interregional hatred, a verdict he called "absurd." Kyrgyz Activist Gets 2 Years For Criticizing Growing Chinese Presence.

item.title: Oil Exports Find A Way Past Iranian Attacks, But Refinery Bottleneck Persists
item.description: Exports of crude oil from the Middle East hit their highest level in September since the war with Iran began, reinforcing a trend of increased supplies despite Iranian attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, according to analysis of shipping and commodity market data by industry observers. Oil Exports Find A Way Past Iranian Attacks, But Refinery Bottleneck Persists.

item.title: Georgia Summons Iranian Ambassador Over Remarks On Revered Queen Ketevan
item.description: Georgia summoned Iran’s ambassador after his planned book Georgia has summoned Iran’s ambassador after his plans to publish a personal interpretation of Queen Ketevan’s history sparked criticism from ruling party lawmakers. Revered as a saint in Georgia, Ketevan was tortured and killed in Persia in the 17th century after refusing to renounce Christianity. Georgia Summons Iranian Ambassador Over Remarks On Revered Queen Ketevan.

item.title: Tbilisi Rebukes Iranian Envoy Over Social Media Post On Canonized Georgian Queen
item.description: Iran’s ambassador to Georgia announced plans to publish research on Queen Ketevan, a 17th-century monarch executed by Persia and later canonized by the Georgian Orthodox Church. Tbilisi summoned the envoy over the move, which the Foreign Ministry viewed as an inappropriate intervention in Georgian religious history. The incident highlights ongoing diplomatic friction between the two nations. Georgia’s government rejected the ambassador’s framing of the historical figure.

item.title: Afghanistan’s TTP sanctuary is becoming harder to deny
item.description: For years, Pakistan’s claim that the Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan operates from sanctuaries inside Afghanistan produced a familiar exchange: Islamabad accused, Kabul denied, and each new militant attack triggered another round of recrimination. That pattern is becoming harder to sustain. The sanctuary dispute can now be tested against a growing body of evidence rather than competing claims [] The p Afghanistan’s TTP sanctuary is becoming harder to deny.

item.title: Nepal floods threaten jobs and livelihoods beyond disaster zone: ILO
item.description: The deadly flash floods in northern Nepal have severely disrupted employment and livelihoods, with wider impacts beyond communities that were directly affected, the International Labour Organization (ILO) said in a preliminary assessment released on Thursday. Nepal floods threaten jobs and livelihoods beyond disaster zone: ILO.

item.title: Ebola response faces setback as transit centre burns down in DR Congo camp
item.description: The enormous challenge of halting the spread of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) just became even harder after a key transit centre for patients requiring treatment burned down in Ituri province. Ebola response faces setback as transit centre burns down in DR Congo camp.

item.title: 'Exhausted' Afghan Refugees Get Extension At Camp In Qatar As US Lawmakers Urge Action
item.description: Qatar will keep the Afghan refugee camp open for another nine months after the closure deadline passed, according to Afghan refugees being held at a camp in Qatar have been told it will be kept open for another nine months after a deadline for its closure passed, but they face continuing uncertainty over their fate amid an ongoing bar on entry to the United States.

item.title: Daredevil Jaan Roose completes slackline walk high above central Seoul
item.description: Estonian slackliner Jaan Roose walked a 160-metre line 120 metres above Seoul on Thursday. The ribbon stretched between the Koreana hotel and Dong-A Media Center near Gyeongbokgung palace. He completed the first of two planned attempts. item.description: Support for white Afrikaners, anti-communism and others reveals how US redefining what qualifies as human rightsWith hours left before the funding expires, the Trump administration is pushing to direct more than $175m of the state department’s flagship human rights fund to a slate of awards that includes a massive $40m grant for an anti-communism fund, support for a group advancing white Afrikaner.

item.title: South African leader urges men to speak up on gender-based violence after series of killings
item.description: President Cyril Ramaphosa urged men to take responsibility for gender-based violence. He announced new measures following a recent wave of murders. Authorities face anger over inadequate protection for women. President announces measures amid anger at authorities over recent murders of womenSouth Africa’s president has called on men to take more responsibility for violence against women as he announced measures to tackle the problem, amid anger at authorities over a recent wave of murders. Cyril Ramaphosa acknowledged that not enough had been done to protect women.
